newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay warns of costs at new airport.
newsitem.headline: Cathay warns of costs at new airport.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd warned of congestion at Hong Kong's existing airport and potentially high costs at the territory's new airport, with the airline industry in general facing tight margins.

"From now until 2000, the industry as a whole will be operating to very tight margins, as fuel prices and over-capacity in the market remain constant concerns," Cathay chairman Peter Sutch said in the airline's annual report.
Sutch said 1997 should bring improvement for Cathay if traffic growth and continuing falls in unit costs could outweigh currency and fuel cost uncertainty.
But he said congestion at Hong Kong's Kai Tak airport would reach its worst levels in 1997, placing severe constraints on Cathay's ability to expand.
Sutch also warned that the new Chek Lap Kok airport would lift the airline's costs. It is scheduled to open in April 1998.

"The opening of the new airport in 1998 is expected to bring increases in our operational costs, and the increased capacity into Hong Kong afforded by the new airport will put pressure on our yields," Sutch said.
However, there were also substantial potential benefits to Hong Kong's airline industry, the economy and community provided the new airport remained competitive, he added.
Sutch said Cathay was hopeful that the opportunities presented by Chek Lap Kok would not be undermined by "excessive landing charges or associated fees".
Cathay has been critical of the new airport's higher costs, and executives have said the carrier would be hardest hit by higher user charges, and might have to cut unprofitable routes.

The new airport's fee structure has yet to be announced by the Airport Authority, which has denied claims by the International Air Transport Association and other user groups that Chek Lap Kok will become one of the world's most expensive.
